title: Basic shapes
sub: Two and three nodes: the building blocks.

graphs.title: Direct effect
graphs.note: S causes Y and nothing else.

graphs.title: Unrelated
graphs.note: Y has a cause; S is not connected to anything.

graphs.title: Mediator
graphs.note: S reaches Y only through M.

graphs.title: Direct and mediated
graphs.note: S reaches Y directly and through M.

graphs.title: Observed confounder
graphs.note: Z causes both S and Y. S has no effect on Y.

graphs.title: Collider
graphs.note: S and Y both cause C, and are independent of each other.

graphs.title: Outcome causes S
graphs.note: The arrow points from Y to S.

graphs.title: Y has a child
graphs.note: S causes Y, and Y causes a later column X.

title: Proxies and admissible paths
sub: A marks a column the analyst allows to carry S's influence; P marks a proxy that is not allowed.

graphs.title: Admissible mediator
graphs.note: S reaches Y only through A.

graphs.title: Admissible plus direct
graphs.note: S reaches Y through A and directly.

graphs.title: Proxy beside admissible
graphs.note: One allowed path through A and one proxy path through P.

graphs.title: Two proxies
graphs.note: Two parallel proxy paths.

graphs.title: Proxy chain
graphs.note: S reaches Y through two proxies in a row.

graphs.title: Proxy feeds admissible
graphs.note: S shapes A through P, and only A touches Y.

graphs.title: Proxy mixes S with a real cause
graphs.note: P is caused by S and by X; only X causes Y.

graphs.title: Admissible collider
graphs.note: A is caused by S and by Z, and Z also causes Y.

title: Hidden variables
sub: Dashed nodes are real causes that never appear as columns.

graphs.title: Hidden confounder
graphs.note: U causes both S and Y; there is no visible edge between them.

graphs.title: Hidden mediator
graphs.note: The only path from S to Y runs through an unrecorded column.

graphs.title: Hidden cause of Y
graphs.note: U adds noise to Y and is unrelated to S.

graphs.title: Hidden confounder plus direct
graphs.note: U causes S and Y, and S also causes Y.

graphs.title: Hidden confounder of a mediator
graphs.note: U causes the mediator M and Y.

graphs.title: Hidden root behind a proxy
graphs.note: U causes S and P; P causes Y.

graphs.title: Recorded label
graphs.note: T is the true quality and is never recorded. Y is the label, and S changes it.

graphs.title: Hidden cause of an admissible column
graphs.note: A is caused by S and by U, and U also causes Y.

graphs.title: Instrument with hidden confounder
graphs.note: I moves S only; U confounds S and Y.

title: Colliders and selection
sub: Shapes where a shared child or a conditioned column opens a path.

graphs.title: M-bias
graphs.note: C is a child of S's cause and of Y's cause.

graphs.title: Butterfly
graphs.note: M-bias where C also causes S and Y.
graphs.edges: Z1>S Z1>C Z2>C Z2>Y C>S C>Y

graphs.title: Shared child plus direct
graphs.note: S causes Y, and both cause C.

graphs.title: Descendant of a collider
graphs.note: S and Y cause C, and C causes D.

graphs.title: Selection record
graphs.note: C records who was selected; it depends on S and Y. X causes Y.

title: Several protected attributes
sub: Two protected columns, as in race and sex.

graphs.title: Two independent attributes
graphs.note: S1 and S2 each cause Y.

graphs.title: One attribute causes another
graphs.note: S1 causes S2, and S2 causes Y.

graphs.title: Intersection through a mediator
graphs.note: S1 and S2 meet in M, which causes Y.

graphs.title: Direct and proxy
graphs.note: S1 causes Y directly; S2 acts through a proxy.

title: After the outcome
sub: Columns recorded after Y, which a downstream model might still use.

graphs.title: Later feature
graphs.note: S reaches Y through X, and Y causes W.

graphs.title: Later feature that also depends on S
graphs.note: W comes after Y and also depends on S.

graphs.title: Outcome as a mediator
graphs.note: S causes Y and a score R; Y causes W, and W also feeds R.

title: Five and six nodes
sub: Combinations of the shapes above, including two shaped like project datasets.

graphs.title: Diamond with a cross link
graphs.note: Two paths from S to Y, with X1 also causing X2.

graphs.title: Census-style
graphs.note: S sex, M marital status, A education, Z age.
graphs.edges: S>M S>A Z>M Z>Y A>Y M>Y

graphs.title: Recidivism-style
graphs.note: S race, Z age, P prior counts.

graphs.title: Front door
graphs.note: U confounds S and Y; all of S's effect passes through M.

graphs.title: Every forward edge
graphs.note: All 10 edges allowed by the order S, A, X, M, Y.
graphs.edges: S>A S>X S>M S>Y A>X A>M A>Y X>M X>Y M>Y

graphs.title: Confounded chain
graphs.note: Each link of S to M to Y has its own observed confounder.
graphs.edges: Z1>S Z1>M Z2>M Z2>Y S>M M>Y

graphs.title: Proxy, admissible and hidden
graphs.note: U causes the proxy P and Y.
graphs.edges: S>A A>Y S>P P>Y U>P U>Y

graphs.title: Isolated S in a rich world
graphs.note: Four columns shape Y; S touches none of them.

graphs.title: Two routes, one hidden
graphs.note: S reaches Y through A and through M then X; U causes A and Y.
graphs.edges: S>A A>Y S>M M>X X>Y U>A U>Y
